title: Invite governance: domain verification and email allowlist/denylist for org & team admin flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Implement tightened org and team invite controls to meet enterprise security requirements. Deliverables: (1) Domain verification flow for org owners (DNS TXT + email TXT fallback), (2) Org-level email allowlist and denylist enforcement with optional team-level overrides, (3) Invite policy modes: open, allowlist-only, SSO-only, and approval-required, (4) Audit logging of all invite events (create, resend, accept, revoke) with actor, IP, and SSO assertion, (5) API endpoints for programmatic management and a console UX for admins.
background_and_motivation: Enterprise customers are asking for stronger controls to prevent account sprawl and unverified email signups. Recent pilot feedback from two finance customers indicated domain verification + denylist support is a blocking requirement for Private deployment. This work complements RBAC v2 by ensuring team membership changes are auditable and policy-driven.
design_considerations:
- Domain verification: primary method is DNS TXT; fallback email verification for domains without DNS access. Store verification status as an organization property used by invite logic.
- Allowlist/denylist: support exact address and wildcard domain entries (e.g., *@partner.com). Denylist takes precedence over allowlist.
- SSO interaction: if org is SSO-only, invites are disabled and admin can send 'SSO onboarding' links instead. If domain is verified and SSO configured, auto-approve invites from that domain.
- Team overrides: teams may opt-in to stricter allowlist only; propagation logic must not relax org-level deny entries.
- Audit logging: use existing audit pipeline spec. Log structure: event, actor_id, target_email, invite_id, ip, timestamp, method (API/Console), sso_provider (if present), reason (if admin-provided). Logs must be immutable and forwarded to customer auditors when on Private.
- UX: single admin surface under Organization Settings > Security > Invite policies; team-level toggles under Team Settings.
acceptance_criteria: Domain verification flow implemented and tested (DNS + email fallback)
Invite policies include open / allowlist-only / SSO-only / approval-required modes
Email allowlist and denylist support exact and wildcard rules; denylist precedence enforced
Invite audit events emitted for create/resend/accept/revoke with required fields
API endpoints: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE for allowlist/denylist and invite policies documented
Console UI screens for org and team invite controls implemented and e2e tested
Security review completed and sign-off from Security and Compliance teams
implementation_notes:
- Backend: new tables invite_policies, domain_verifications, email_lists; consider reuse of existing org_settings table to minimize migrations.
- AuthZ: integrate with RBAC v2 so only Org Owners and Admins can modify org-wide policies; team-level toggles restricted to Team Admin role.
- Audit pipeline: hook into audit service (ENG-4690) and include telemetry metric for blocked invites count.
- Migration: default behavior for existing orgs is to preserve current open invites; add a migration job to mark domains as 'unverified' until verification flow completes.
- Rate limiting: throttle domain verification attempts to 5 per hour per org to avoid abuse.
- Backwards compatibility: API v1 invites remain functional but will surface new policy fields; document breaking changes in API changelog.
- Testing: unit tests for policy resolution, integration tests for SSO interaction, e2e for console flows, and privacy review for email fallback content.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Email fallback for domain verification increases attack surface (temporary tokens sent to random addresses). Mitigation: short-lived tokens, limited retries, and logging.
- Allowlist wildcards may unintentionally accept addresses (e.g., *@corp.com vs *@corp.co). Mitigation: exact match precedence and validation helper for common wildcard mistakes.
- Strict denylist policies may cause onboarding friction for legitimate contractors. Mitigation: approval-required mode for exceptional cases and clear admin notifications.
- SSO-only mode prevents external collaborator invites; workaround: explicit guest access flows tied to identity provider guest accounts.
